'''John Henry Schwarz''' (Born November 22, 1941) is an American [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.theory.caltech.edu/people/jhs/cv.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2010-04-03 |archive-date=2011-06-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607035210/http://www.theory.caltech.edu/people/jhs/cv.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> Along with [[Yoichiro Nambu]], [[Holger Bech Nielsen]], [[Joël Scherk]], [[Gabriele Veneziano]], [[Michael Green (physicist)|Michael Green]], and [[Leonard Susskind]], he is regarded as one of the founders of [[string theory]].

==Early life and education==
He studied mathematics at [[Harvard College]] ([[Bachelor of Arts|A.B.]], 1962) and theoretical physics at the [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California at Berkeley]] ([[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]], 1966), where his graduate advisor was [[Geoffrey Chew]].
For several years he was one of the very few physicists who pursued [[string theory]] as a viable theory of [[quantum gravity]].

His work with [[Michael Green (physicist)|Michael Green]] on [[Green–Schwarz mechanism|anomaly cancellation in Type I string theories]] led to the so-called "[[first superstring revolution]]" of 1984, which greatly contributed to moving string theory into the mainstream of research in theoretical physics.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://superstringtheory.com/people/johns.html |title=superstringtheory.com |access-date=2010-12-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160909152412/http://www.superstringtheory.com/people/johns.html |archive-date=2016-09-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Schwarz was an [[assistant professor]] at [[Princeton University]] from 1966 to 1972.  He then moved to the [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech), where he is currently the [[Harold Brown (Secretary of Defense)|Harold Brown]] Professor of Theoretical Physics.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://theory.caltech.edu/~jhs/ |title=Faculty website |access-date=2004-11-25 |archive-date=2004-12-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041203001627/http://theory.caltech.edu/~jhs/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Awards==
He was elected a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] and a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] (1986).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1986&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=ARS|access-date=23 September 2020}}</ref> He was a fellow of the [[MacArthur Foundation]] in 1987.

He received the [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|Dirac Medal]] of the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] in 1989, and the [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics]] of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2002. On December 12, 2013, he shared the Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics with Michael Green "for opening new perspectives on quantum gravity and the unification of forces."
